newsitem.title: ECUADOR: President of Ecuador state telecom firm quits.
newsitem.headline: President of Ecuador state telecom firm quits.

text.p: A cousin of Ecuador's recently fired President Abdala Bucaram resigned Tuesday as head of state telephone company Emetel.
"I have presented my resignation," Rene Bucaram told reporters. "I don't know anything at all about communications. I was in Emetel to clean the company up."
Bucaram said he had uncovered evidence of corruption in Emetel before he took over the company in January and detected 281 irregular contracts.
"I have appointed a commission to investigate the contracts," he said, "There are going to be some people who will have to go to jail."
The Ecuadorean government hopes to raise $1 billion through the privatization of a third of Emetel, which is due by the end of April.
U.S. firms MCI Communications Corp and GTE Corp have presented documentation to participate in the privatization, as have Italy's Stet SpA, Spain's Telefonica de Espana, and Korea Telecom.
Abdala Bucaram was dismissed by Congress on the grounds of "mental incompetence" February 6.
